html:
A treaty of the Council of Europe, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950, that protects basic rights and lets individuals take their own governments to an international court. It came into force in 1953.

It was written after the Second World War, the Nazi crimes and the Holocaust, and as communism spread in Eastern Europe. Its authors wanted to keep Western Europe's democracies from sliding back into dictatorship. It drew on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948, but made the rights enforceable.

It protects the right to life, a fair trial, privacy and family life, freedom of thought, speech and assembly, and bans torture, slavery and discrimination. The European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg, from 1959, hears cases. Since 1998 any person in a member state can bring a case directly after exhausting the courts at home.

It is separate from the European Union. Membership grew to nearly every European state after the Cold War. Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe in 2022 after it invaded Ukraine.
sum: A treaty of the Council of Europe, signed in Rome on 4 November 1950, that protects basic rights and lets individuals take their own governments to an international court. It came into force in 1953.
